lessons.title: Prepositions of place
lessons.objective: By the end, learners can describe where people and things are.
lessons.explanation: Use in for an enclosed space, on for a surface and under for a lower position.
examples: The keys are on the table.
The bag is under the chair.

lessons.title: Present Perfect and Past Simple
lessons.objective: By the end, learners can choose between a life experience and a finished past time.
lessons.explanation: Use Present Perfect when the time is unfinished or not stated. Use Past Simple with a finished time such as last year.

lessons.title: Restaurant English
lessons.objective: By the end, learners can order food and handle a simple restaurant conversation.
lessons.explanation: Use polite requests such as Could I have…? and ask for the bill when you are ready to pay.
examples: Could I have the menu, please?
Use the pattern in a short real-life sentence.

lessons.title: Reading: evidence and inference
lessons.objective: By the end, learners can make a supported inference from a short text.
lessons.explanation: An inference must be supported by details in the text; do not choose an answer based only on outside knowledge.
lessons.reading: The community library extended its opening hours after a survey showed that many residents worked late. Three months later, evening attendance had doubled, while daytime attendance remained stable. The library now plans to add more study desks rather than reduce its daytime services.
examples: Look for a detail that supports each conclusion.
Use the pattern in a short real-life sentence.
nextSteps: Try the related practice in your dashboard.

practice.prompt: Why did the library extend its hours?
practice.why: The text directly gives this reason. This is the correct evidence choice.

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Try again and check the clue.

practice.prompt: What can we infer about evening attendance?
practice.why: The text says it doubled. This is the correct evidence choice.

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Try again and check the clue.

practice.prompt: What will the library probably do next?
practice.why: The final sentence states this plan. This is the correct evidence choice.

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Try again and check the clue.

practice.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the passage?
options: A schedule change responded to residents' needs.
A library moved to a new building.
A survey measured only daytime visitors.
practice.why: This combines the reason, change and result. This is the correct evidence choice.

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Try again and check the clue.

practice.prompt: What does ‘stable’ mean in the passage?
practice.why: Daytime attendance remained stable, so it did not change much. This is the correct evidence choice.

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Try again and check the clue.

lessons.readingText: Look for evidence; an inference is not directly stated, but it is supported by details.
